outcome_90: Prove the repeatable MACS Client Zero loop: durable business intake → portable ICM client brain → isolated tenant context → approval-gated AI action → verified evidence/export, so the same process can be sold to Client #1.
constraints: Do not replace working systems merely to simplify the stack. Preserve client ownership of code, domains, hosting, databases, credentials and data. No cross-client context leakage. No consequential AI write/send/publish/delete/spend without enforced human approval.
proof: Intake survives restart; a memoryless agent can cold-walk the MACS business context; two-tenant isolation is proven; agent writes have zero side effects before approval; approval executes once; rejection has no side effect; client context/data can be exported; rollback is documented and rehearsed.
economic_value: Create a sellable, repeatable diagnosis-and-implementation process that reduces custom discovery work while producing verified client outcomes and a clear path to recurring MAXX Operations.
offers: Offer 01 — The Sovereign Business System: audit/diagnosis, a 90-day adaptive implementation partnership, sovereign key handoff, and optional ongoing operations.
primary_customer: Initial niche: sports and basketball programs; coaches, mentors, youth programs and community organizations; minority-owned small businesses; adjacent nontechnical small businesses needing better lead, customer, marketing, funding or operating systems.
bottleneck: The commercial promise is clearer than the current verified runtime. Client Zero must prove durable intake, tenant isolation, enforced approvals, portable context and a cold-walk handoff before stronger software claims are sold.
brand_promise: MACS spends 90 days learning the business, fixing digital bottlenecks that cost time or money, installing an owner-controlled business system, and handing over the keys.
voice: Plainspoken, outcome-first, human, nontechnical, precise, anti-hype. Explain business results before AI architecture. Do not fabricate proof or imply capabilities are live when they are not.
forbidden_claims: Do not claim every customer needs AI, a new website, a CRM replacement or a predetermined automation bundle. Do not claim unverified grant/browser automation, production Postiz operations, proven tenant isolation or enforced approval gates until evidence exists.
tenant_isolation: Each client/company receives an isolated tenant/namespace. Reusable structure, policies and adapters may be shared; private records, credentials, conversations, customer lists and proprietary content may not cross tenants.
model_policy: Company context must remain portable and model-agnostic. Models are replaceable consumers of authorized context, not the canonical home of the business.
handoff: Client receives organized portable context, process/bottleneck map, implemented systems, evidence, owner access, exports, cold-walk operating instructions, human-judgment list and optional operations proposal.
workflow_one: Client Zero Loop: capture a MACS inquiry/intake durably, normalize it to ICM context, enforce tenant isolation, propose one benign CRM write, require explicit approval/rejection, execute at most once, log evidence, and export the resulting client context.
trigger: A new business audit/intake submission is received.
workflow_output: A durable, tenant-scoped client brain plus a verified approval-gated action record and exportable evidence bundle.
approval_matrix: Consequential writes, sends, publishing, deletion, money, credentials, production changes and policy changes require explicit human approval. The agent may research, summarize, classify and propose within authorized read scope.
abstention: Abstain/escalate when context is missing or contradictory, tenant identity is uncertain, requested authority is absent, evidence is stale, a consequential action lacks approval, or rollback cannot be established.
audit_log: Record actor/delegating human, tenant, timestamp, trigger/event, retrieved evidence, policy decision, proposed action, approval/rejection, execution idempotency key, result, verification and rollback reference.
incident_owner: Stacy McSwain for MACS business decisions; platform-level production/security intervention remains with the authorized system owner/administrator.
